Phase 2 (fix) — MERGED. Gerrit change 2381 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2381) landed at patch set 5 (server-rebased on Submit), merge commit a36c7407bfcf, with LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.

FINAL FIX (localized; 130 non-test LOC across src/rebar/review_bot/app.py + config.py). Restores ADR 0067's PROCESS-level "shutdown <= drain + cancel" bound that c2ba claimed but never delivered:
- app.py: on shutdown, after the bounded cancel, arm a DAEMON threading.Timer that calls `_force_process_exit` (os._exit) — the only thing that forces the process down past an orphaned, un-force-cancellable `asyncio.to_thread` OS thread (neither `asyncio.run`'s `shutdown_default_executor` join NOR interpreter finalization can cancel a busy non-daemon thread; both JOIN it — empirically confirmed).
- GATED on a real orphan: the lifespan installs its OWN default executor (`thread_name_prefix="reviewbot-offload"`) at startup, and the arm fires only when a live non-daemon `reviewbot-offload_*` thread survives the cancel. A clean shutdown with no offload is never armed.
- Source-derived, lock-safe grace: `config.shutdown_force_exit_grace_seconds()` = store lock budget (lock._DEFAULT_TIMEOUT*_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=60) + git timeout (30) = 90s = the max time an abandoned `event_append` store write needs to RELEASE its mkdir write-lock, so os._exit NEVER preempts a legit bounded write (no orphaned lock dir). drain(1200)+cancel(10)+grace(90)=1300 < stop_grace_period(1320), so the controlled, logged exit fires before Docker's own (unreliable) SIGKILL — the AC1 port-release guarantee, i.e. the actual 2026-08-28 ~22-min zombie.
- Logs `logger.critical` naming surviving offload threads before os._exit (operator signal in journald).

RED->GREEN oracle (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py):
- test_shutdown_forces_process_exit_when_an_orphaned_to_thread_review_outlives_cancel — drives a REAL orphaned to_thread at shutdown; asserts the force-down ACTION via an injected seam (not a stopwatch). RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix.
- test_clean_shutdown_with_no_orphaned_offload_does_not_force_process_exit — a normal shutdown with no offload must NOT force-exit (the gate's other half).
- test_force_exit_deadline_stays_within_the_stop_grace_band (config tier) — pins drain+cancel+grace < stop_grace_period AND grace >= lock budget, read from source so raising any budget fails CI.

MUTATION (teeth, all caught): (1) remove the arm -> firing test RED; (2) ungate (always-arm) -> clean test RED; (3) no-op the prefixed-executor install -> firing test RED (proves the install is load-bearing: without it the orphan runs on a generic asyncio_ thread the gate cannot distinguish).

REVIEW ITERATION: LLM-Review -1 on PS1 (3 findings: no log; fixed 5s grace ungated/lock-unsafe; no clean-teardown test) — all three addressed. Two CI worker-crash failures then root-caused and fixed: (a) the force-exit seam was neutralized only in test_review_bot.py, so other lifespan-driving tests armed a real os._exit that killed an xdist worker — moved the neutralizer into repo-wide tests/conftest.py; (b) the gate scanned the GENERIC `asyncio_` prefix, so an unrelated to_thread thread from another xdist test falsely tripped it — fixed by the dedicated `reviewbot-offload` prefix. PS4 CI: py3.11/3.12/3.13 all green.

STEP 7 sibling sweep: only two FastAPI lifespans (review_bot, opcert_service). opcert_service already fixed the SAME class (bug c89f) via an app-owned executor abandoned on shutdown — not left with the identical defect. No other uvicorn lifespan services.

Attribution: caused_by -> c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a (melting-resting-serpent), class plan_defect. c2ba bounded only the asyncio await, not the process, so the ADR-0067 process-level bound was introduced-but-incomplete (a plan defect, not a regression). The fix completes that already-accepted design — a localized code fix, not an escalation.

Closing with close_class=plan_defect, caused_by=c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a.
